title: A Derandomization Framework for Structure Discovery: Applications in Neural Networks and Beyond
claim: With tiny perturbations the optimum stays nonzero and decays with regularization, while the exact stationary point sits at zero.
layout: 1 line plot, 4 curves, legend top-right, red marked point at origin
description: A single line plot titled 'Optimal w* and Curves for Different λ and ρ'. The x-axis is the regularization parameter λ from 0 to 1. The y-axis is the optimal w*, from 0 to about 0.007. A solid black horizontal line at w* = 0 represents ρ = 0, the exact second-order stationary point. A small red circle marks the origin on this line. Three dashed curves in blue, orange and green stand for ρ = 0.0001, 0.0002 and 0.0003. Each curve starts high at small λ and drops steeply toward zero as λ grows. Larger ρ gives a higher curve, and the green curve peaks near 0.007. The legend sits in the upper right. The eye goes first to the steep dashed curves in the upper left, then to the flat black baseline.
caption: Optimal \(w\) vs. \(\lambda\) for \(f(w, b) = \mathbb{E}[(ReLU^3(wx+b) - 1)^2] + \lambda w^2\) when biases are trained. The solid line shows convergence to 0 at an exact SOSP.
abstract: Understanding the dynamics of feature learning in neural networks (NNs) remains a significant challenge. The work of (Mousavi-Hosseini et al., 2023) analyzes a multiple index teacher-student setting and shows that a two-layer student attains a low-rank structure in its first-layer weights when trained with stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and a strong regularizer. This structural property is known to reduce sample complexity of generalization. Indeed, in a second step, the same authors establish algorithm-specific learning guarantees under additional assumptions. In this paper, we focus exclusively on the structure discovery aspect and study it under weaker assumptions, more specifically: we allow (a) NNs of arbitrary size and depth, (b) with all parameters trainable, (c) under any smooth loss function, (d) tiny regularization, and (e) trained by any method that attains a second-order stationary point (SOSP), e.g.\ perturbed gradient descent (PGD). At the core of our approach is a key $\textit{derandomization}$ lemma, which states that optimizing the function $\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{x}} \left[g_Î¸(\mathbf{W}\mathbf{x} + \mathbf{b})\right]$ converges to a point where $\mathbf{W} = \mathbf{0}$, under mild conditions. The fundamental nature of this lemma directly explains structure discovery and has immediate applications in other domains including an end-to-end approximation for MAXCUT, and computing Johnson-Lindenstrauss embeddings.
